subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 20, 2026
body:
Emacs 31.1 has been released, bringing a long list of changes to the popular editor, including the removal of the old Emacs Lisp compiler and many other improvements. This update is now available to AcreetionOS users through the Arch repositories, and can be easily installed using pacman, highlighting the benefits of our distribution's close tracking of upstream packages.

Development
The AcreetionOS continuous integration pipeline has been refined with the addition of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, making our ISO build process more reliable and efficient. This enhancement is a testament to our community's dedication to improving the workflow and ensuring that users receive the most up-to-date and stable versions of AcreetionOS, which can be found on our website at https://acreetionos.org/. For more information on the latest changes, you can check out our changelog at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Community
The AcreetionOS community has been active in discussing the latest security updates, including the recent stable kernel set, which includes versions 7.1.10 and 6.18.46. You can find more information about these updates and how to apply them on our wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html. Additionally, our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html provides detailed guides on how to use and configure AcreetionOS, including how to keep your system up to date with the latest security patches. If you're looking for the latest ISO image, you can find it at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.
